assessment.levelDescription: Catastrophic event: active ransomware, examination leak, financial breach, or widespread campus network compromise. Requires immediate KENET-CERT escalation.

itTeamPlaybook.action: Validate Incident Scope (1 Hour (Immediate Emergency Protocol))
itTeamPlaybook.details: Assigned SLA is 1 hour(s). Verify reporter identity, check SIEM / syslog correlation for affected asset [FINANCE_ERP].
Place affected IP / MAC on the isolated quarantine VLAN. Push dynamic firewall block rule at campus perimeter edge gateway.
Force Kerberos ticket-granting service (TGS) reset in Active Directory and revoke refresh tokens on Azure AD / Office 365 tenant.

itTeamPlaybook.action: Volatile RAM & Master Boot Record (MBR) Extraction
itTeamPlaybook.details: Capture memory dump using LiME / FTK Imager CLI before re-imaging. Extract sample hash and cross-reference with VirusTotal / Hybrid-Analysis.
Verify shadow copies and restore affected partition from verified offline backup taken prior to initial compromise date.
Compile Root Cause Analysis report within 5 business days. Update firewall rules and schedule targeted cybersecurity awareness training.

reporterActions.details: Immediately unplug the Ethernet network cable or turn off Wi-Fi on the affected computer. Do NOT power off the computer as volatile RAM contains critical forensic evidence.

reporterActions.action: DO NOT pay any ransom or communicate with extortionists
reporterActions.details: Paying ransom never guarantees decryption and violates university cybersecurity policy. IT retains offline backups.
Take a clear photograph of the ransom screen showing the exact Bitcoin address, extension, and transaction ID for the forensic dossier.

reporterActions.action: Do not plug in USB flash drives
reporterActions.details: Avoid connecting personal flash drives or external hard drives to avoid spreading malware to other computers or home devices.

complianceActions.action: Submit Higher Education Incident Notification Form
complianceActions.details: KENET-CERT facilitates inter-university threat telemetry sharing and ISP coordination. Submit incident artifact dossier.
Escalate to the National Kenya Computer Incident Response Team under the Communications Authority of Kenya (CA).

title: Whistleblower Report: Examination Papers Shared on Social Media Group
description: Screenshots of upcoming semester examinations uploaded to private Telegram channel 'Campus Past Papers & Leaks 2026'. PDFs contain lecturer review watermarks.

assessment.levelDescription: Severe academic integrity crisis: exam compromise requires immediate exam re-setting and forensic investigation.

triageNotes.text: Academic Registrar alerted immediately. Exam cancelled and replacement papers requisitioned. Workstation audit commenced.
triageNotes.author: Kenneth Ochieng

title: Ransomware (LockBit Variant) Outbreak in Computer Science Lab 4
description: 18 desktop workstations in Lab 4 displayed black extortion screens demanding 0.5 BTC. File extensions renamed to '.locked'. Student project repositories and local virtual machines encrypted.
indicators: Malware file: update_service.exe, Ransom note: RESTORE_FILES.txt, C2 IP: 91.240.118.12

assessment.levelDescription: Active ransomware encryption on lab systems. Immediate network isolation enforced.

triageNotes.text: VLAN 24 isolated at switch level. Memory dump acquired from Lab-PC-07. No lateral movement detected into faculty server cluster.
triageNotes.author: Grace Wanjiku

title: Counterfeit University Fee Subsidy & M-PESA Phishing Portal
description: Mass SMS and WhatsApp messages circulating among students claiming to offer a 50% university tuition fee subsidy via a spoofed domain 'campus-fees-portal.com'. Several students entered their portal admission numbers and M-PESA transaction PINs.
indicators: Phishing URL: http://campus-fees-portal.com/pay, SMS Sender: 'CAMPUS-FINANCE', Target IP: 185.220.101.44

assessment.levelDescription: High risk of student financial loss and credential theft across campus.

triageNotes.text: Phishing domain blocked on campus edge gateway. Abuse report filed with registrar. Advisory broadcast sent via student portal.
triageNotes.author: Alex Kimani

title: Rogue 'Evil Twin' Wi-Fi Hotspot Broadcasting in Main Campus Library
description: An open Wi-Fi network named 'CAMPUS_FREE_STUDENT_WIFI' was detected in the library 2nd floor. Connecting presented a counterfeit captive portal asking students for their email passwords.
indicators: BSSID: 00:14:22:98:AA:BC, Signal Strength: -48 dBm near Carrel Desk 14, Captive Portal IP: 192.168.4.1

assessment.levelDescription: Active MITM rogue AP attempting credential harvesting in localized campus zone.

triageNotes.text: Campus security located a battery-powered rogue device concealed under study furniture. Confiscated for forensic analysis.
triageNotes.author: Alex Kimani

title: Unauthorized Access and Grade Alteration Attempt on Exam Server
description: Database audit logs triggered alerts for modified SQL records on table `tbl_unit_marks` without lecturer digital signature. SQL injection flaw leveraged via faculty marks entry module.
indicators: Attacker IP: 197.232.88.19 (Public Proxy), Compromised Account: staff_lecturer_49

assessment.levelDescription: Direct integrity threat to academic grading and university certification credibility.

triageNotes.text: Compromised lecturer account disabled. Database rolled back to clean snapshot. Disciplinary committee notified.
triageNotes.author: Kenneth Ochieng

title: DDoS Traffic Flood against Student ERP during Semester Unit Registration
description: Inbound HTTP SYN and UDP flood exceeding 18 Gbps targeted portal.campus.ac.ke, rendering the registration portal unresponsive on deadline day for over 4,000 students.
indicators: Target Port: 443, Inbound Bandwidth: 18.4 Gbps, Attack Vector: DNS Amplification and NTP Reflection

assessment.levelDescription: Major availability outage during high-impact academic deadline.

triageNotes.text: DDoS scrubbing activated with upstream ISP. BGP routes rerouted via protected path. Registration deadline extended by 48 hours.
triageNotes.author: Sarah Chebet

title: Faculty Laptop Stolen Containing Unencrypted Postgraduate Research Data
description: Faculty laptop stolen from departmental office overnight. Laptop contained non-anonymized demographic survey data, student marks, and research proposals.
indicators: Device Serial: 4K9L8Z2, MAC: D4:BE:D9:12:34:56, BitLocker: Not Enabled

assessment.levelDescription: Loss of physical hardware containing unencrypted personal identifiable information.

triageNotes.text: Remote wipe command issued via Microsoft Intune MDM. Microsoft 365 session revoked. Incident report logged.
triageNotes.author: Grace Wanjiku

title: Cryptomining Daemon Installed on High-Performance Research Cluster
description: CPU utilization on cluster node 'hpc-node-03' spiked to 100%. Process `kswapd0` was masquerading as a kernel worker but executing XMRig Monero miner via a hijacked SSH key.

assessment.levelDescription: Unauthorized consumption of computational power with compromised SSH credentials.

triageNotes.text: Process killed, malicious cronjob purged. SSH keys rotated, root login disabled.
triageNotes.author: Vincent Barasa
